content:
Hi, I'm Octavian Halmaghi. I trained as a mathematician and have worked for the last
20 years as a software developer. I've been using Lean since Lean 4 came out.

For the past months I've been formalizing Audin–Damian, "Morse Theory and Floer Homology" both parts, Morse theory (ch. 1–4) and Floer homology / the Arnold
conjecture (ch. 5–16). Every chapter has Lean statements, with a blueprint and a
dependency graph.
14 sorries remain, all in ch. 6–7 (elliptic regularity for the
Floer equation, and π₁(Sp(2n)) ≅ ℤ).
Repo: https://github.com/t4v1/damian_formalizare

Along the way I ran into standard results that Mathlib doesn't have: polar
coordinates for lintegral (#43904), Morrey's inequality (#43905), Riesz–Schauder
(#43906, closed), Weyl's lemma for ∂̄, and a few more (Brouwer, Borsuk–Ulam, the
Morse lemma).
I think to contribute the results as 3 PRs (#43904,#43905,#43906)
My question is how you'd like me to proceed. Should #43904 (84 lines) go through
review first as a test? Should I discuss each result here before opening a PR?
Or is this better kept in a separate repo that depends on Mathlib? I'm happy to
answer design questions on the open PRs myself.
